children: said Sunday that its experimental combination treatment for chronic hepatitis delta met its primary goal in a phase 3 clinical trial, while separate phase 2 results showed sustained suppression of the virus in patients who stopped treatment.

In the phase 3 Eclipse 1 trial, 44% of patients receiving elebsiran and tobevibart had undetectable levels of hepatitis delta virus and normalized liver enzyme levels after 48 weeks. That compared with none of the patients in a delayed-treatment control group assessed after 12 weeks.
The findings represent a potential regulatory milestone for Vir

, which is developing the treatment for a serious liver disease with limited therapeutic options. The company plans to seek U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval in mid-2027, potentially creating a new commercial opportunity if regulators determine the treatment is safe and effective.

Chronic hepatitis delta is a viral infection that occurs in people with hepatitis B and can accelerate liver damage, including cirrhosis, or permanent scarring of the liver. The disease also increases the risk of liver failure and liver cancer.

The Eclipse 1 study enrolled 124 patients, including people with advanced liver disease. Among those receiving the combination, 79% had no detectable virus after 48 weeks. The treatment was generally well tolerated, although one patient experienced a temporary reduction in infection-fighting white blood cells.

separately reported updated results from its phase 2 Solstice trial, in which all 28 patients who completed 96 weeks of combination treatment had undetectable virus levels. Among 27 patients evaluated for liver stiffness, 89% showed improvement or stabilization, suggesting reduced inflammation or scarring.

Early findings also raised the possibility that some patients could eventually stop treatment without the virus returning. Ten patients discontinued therapy after sustained viral suppression, and all remained virus-free 12 weeks later. Seven maintained that response through 24 weeks, while one reached 48 weeks. The small sample and limited follow-up mean a lasting cure hasn't been established.

Elebsiran works by interfering with genetic instructions that help hepatitis B produce a protein needed by hepatitis delta. Tobevibart is a laboratory-made antibody designed to block viral entry into liver cells. Both drugs are administered through monthly injections under the skin.

Vir expects additional phase 3 results from its Eclipse 2 and Eclipse 3 studies in the first quarter of 2027. The FDA has granted the combination breakthrough therapy and fast track designations, which may accelerate development and regulatory review but don't guarantee approval.
